title: Kenyan Stuffed Chapati
community: Popular in urban Kenya — a street food and home favourite
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Stuffed Chapati — a chapati dough encasing a spiced filling of egg, vegetables, or minced meat, then rolled thin and pan-fried until golden. Kenya's most satisfying street breakfast — a complete meal in a flatbread.
longDesc: Stuffed chapati takes the already beloved Kenyan chapati and transforms it into a complete meal. The dough is rolled thin, topped with a spiced filling — usually egg, onions, and vegetables — then sealed and cooked on a flat pan. The result is something between a chapati and an omelette, crispy on the outside and rich with filling within. At Nairobi street stalls, it is one of the most popular breakfast choices.
steps: Make chapati dough: combine flour, salt, sugar, and 2 tbsp oil. Add warm water and knead for 8—10 minutes. Rest covered for 1 hour.
Mix all filling ingredients together. Set aside.
Divide dough into 6 balls. Roll each ball very thin on a floured surface.
Heat a flat pan over medium heat. Lightly brush with oil.
Place a rolled chapati on the pan. Cook for 30 seconds until small bubbles appear.
Quickly pour 2—3 tbsp of the egg filling onto the chapati surface. Spread evenly.
Use a spatula to fold the chapati over the filling.
Press down gently. Cook for 2—3 minutes until golden.
Flip carefully. Cook the other side for 2 minutes until golden.
chefTips: The egg filling goes on while the chapati is on the pan — this cooks the bottom while the filling sets.
Pour the filling while the chapati is still slightly soft — before it sets completely.
A meat filling variation: replace the egg with spiced minced beef cooked and cooled.
commonMistakes: Too much filling — the chapati cannot be folded without splitting.
Filling too wet — the chapati becomes soggy rather than crispy.

faqs.q: Can I use a meat filling?
faqs.a: Yes — minced beef or chicken cooked with onions, tomatoes, and spices works beautifully. Cool the filling completely before using and keep the quantity modest so the chapati can fold properly.

cookingScience: The egg mixture is added while the chapati is on the pan so the base heat cooks the bottom of the egg immediately, helping it adhere to the chapati surface before folding. This prevents the filling from sliding out when the chapati is folded.
sustainabilityTips: Stuffed chapati transforms simple eggs and vegetables into a complete, satisfying meal — maximum nutrition from minimal ingredients.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate for up to 1 day.
reheating: Warm in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.
culturalNote: Stuffed chapati is one of the great Kenyan street breakfast foods — found at kiosks and food stalls across Nairobi and other urban centres, where it is prepared fresh to order and eaten standing up.
